_comment: Per-claim search boxes for harness/counterexample.py. These live here, in
the reference tree, because the box a 'no counterexample' result came from
is part of what that result means: over [0, bound] in each Nat variable,
with existential witnesses hunted up to exists_bound. A small bound is not
dishonest, but it must be visible, so raising or lowering one is a change
to the committed record and shows up in review.
A bound is not free. The search EVALUATES the statement's decision
procedure at every point of the box, so a claim about primality of
2^(2^n)+1 cannot be searched past n = 5 on any ordinary machine: n = 6 is
2^64+1, whose trial division is ~2^32 steps. That is why FERMAT-CLAIM's
bound is 5 and not 24 -- and n = 5 is exactly where the claim dies, which
is the whole point of the pair.

FERMAT-CLAIM.why: F_6 = 2^64+1 cannot be decided by the trial division in Nat.Prime's instance. The historical counterexample is at n = 5, inside this box.

FERMAT-F5.why: The statement has no Nat variable: it is about one number. The box is the single empty tuple.

PRIMES.why: The conclusion is an unbounded existential (a prime at least n), so the search can only CONFIRM it by finding a witness; exists_bound has to exceed the largest prime gap below the bound.

PL-BOGUS.falsity_not_searchable: PL-BOGUS is false because p1 -> p1 IS derivable from A1 and A2 by modus ponens, so the first conjunct of Independent fails. That is a fact about derivability in an inductively defined calculus, not about any finite box of numbers: `PL.Derives` has no Decidable instance and a bounded numeric search cannot reach it. Refuting it mechanically needs a bounded DERIVATION search, which this program does not implement (ROADMAP 5.1). Until then the falsity of this control rests on the reviewer's reading, and this search contributes nothing to it.
PL-BOGUS.why: No Nat variable; the search is expected to be NOT_SEARCHABLE and the waiver above says why.
